content.title: So Much Busyness, So Many Achievements—Yet Why Does This Emptiness Remain Within?
content.subtitle: Our souls tire as we forget our purpose and chase our desires.
content.body:
We wake up to the sound of an alarm and step into the familiar rush of daily life—work or business demands, family responsibilities, studies, deadlines, monthly expenses, and finally collapsing into bed with an exhausted body. This mechanical routine feels like an endless cycle, carrying us from childhood toward old age. Yet, on a quiet night or in a moment alone, does an unfamiliar ache suddenly arise within? Do you ever wonder why we came into this world? Is life merely this endless struggle to fulfill our own and our family’s needs? Or have we forgotten an ultimate truth amid the noise of everyday life?

The Ultimate Purpose of Creation and Our Confusion

Allah Subhanahu wa Ta‘ala has clearly stated the fundamental purpose of our existence in the Holy Qur’an: “I did not create jinn and mankind except to worship Me.” (Surah Adh-Dhariyat: 56)

Yet our greatest confusion lies in understanding the meaning of worship. We assume that performing a few rak‘ahs of Salah and fasting during Ramadan fulfills our obligations to Allah. The rest of the time, we believe we can follow the whims of our desires, society, and careers.

The True Essence of Worship and Servitude to the Self

In reality, worship is not merely a set of outward rituals; it means acknowledging our Lord’s Oneness and sovereignty in every step of life. When we place our own desires or society’s norms above Allah’s commands, we unknowingly become caught in a silent epidemic. When creation forgets its Creator and runs after the approval of others, it loses sight of its original purpose.

An Uncompromising Declaration on the Burning Sands

Hazrat Bilal (RA) left behind an extraordinary example of how to embody the purpose of creation. In Makkah at that time, he was a powerless Black slave. But through the light of Tawheed, he understood that no human being deserves our ultimate submission; only Allah does.

On the scorching desert sands, he was whipped with a massive stone pressing against his chest. Umayyah demanded just one thing: praise for the idols. Bilal (RA) knew that his skin might tear, but the tongue created to testify to Tawheed could never praise anyone besides Allah. So, amid unbearable pain, he declared, “Ahad, Ahad!” (Allah is One, Allah is One). This unwavering faith elevated a slave to the extraordinary honor of having the Messenger of Allah ﷺ hear his footsteps in Jannah.

The Invisible Stone Weighing on Our Hearts

Today, the Arabian stone may no longer press against our chests, but something even more dangerous weighs on our hearts: worldly greed and heedlessness toward our Lord’s remembrance. We keep our tongues busy with unnecessary talk and waste hours on social media, yet cannot spare even a few minutes to remember the Lord who created us. Having strayed from our original purpose, we are left with so much emptiness and despair.

The Remedy for Emptiness and Provision for the Final Journey

This profound inner emptiness cannot be filled by worldly achievements; the soul’s thirst can only be quenched by remembering its true Owner. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “The best dhikr is ‘La ilaha illallah.’” (Jami‘ at-Tirmidhi: 3383). These words are more than a momentary movement of the lips; they are a life-giving remedy that cleanses the heart of accumulated doubts, weariness, and the rust of sin.

This dhikr is not only a source of strength throughout life but also a shield at the most critical moment of our final journey. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “Whoever’s final words are ‘La ilaha illallah’ will enter Jannah.” (Sunan Abi Dawud: 3116).

footer_button.hint: To make this life-giving dhikr a living part of our busy lives, Team Muslims Day has launched the ‘La ilaha illallah’ Campaign. Our goal is not merely to complete at least 50 million recitations of this Kalimah in 15 days. More importantly, we want this practice to continue throughout our lives, even after the target has been reached. Whether standing or sitting, during breaks at work, or lying in bed before sleep, may our tongues and hearts never become heedless of our Lord’s remembrance, even for a moment. May our Lord accept this humble effort. Join us on this blessed journey of Tawheed.
